sanskrit: aṅgaś caivaurasaḥ śrīmān rājā bhaumaś ca vīryavān sahasraṃ yaś ca divyānāṃ yugānāṃ paryupāsitā
english: And there was Aṅga, the glorious son begotten of his own loins, and the valiant king Bhauma, who attended through a thousand divine ages.

sanskrit: aryamā caiva bhagavān ye cānye tanayā vibho ete pradeśāḥ kathitā bhuvanānāṃ prabhāvanāḥ
english: And the lord Aryaman too, and whatever other sons there were, O mighty one — these have been declared the regions and the fashioners of the worlds.

sanskrit: śaśabindoś ca bhāryāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi daśācyuta ekaikasyāṃ sahasraṃ tu tanayānām abhūt tadā
english: And of Śaśabindu there were ten thousand wives, O undecaying one, and from each one of them there were then a thousand sons.

sanskrit: evaṃ śatasahasrāṇāṃ śataṃ tasya mahātmanaḥ putrāṇāṃ na ca te kaṃ cid icchanty anyaṃ prajāpatim
english: Thus that great-souled one had a hundred times a hundred thousand sons, and they would acknowledge no other as Lord of Creatures.

sanskrit: prajām ācakṣate viprāḥ paurāṇīṃ śāśabindavīm sa vṛṣṇivaṃśaprabhavo mahān vaṃśaḥ prajāpateḥ
english: The wise call that ancient progeny the Śāśabindava line; that great lineage of the Lord of Creatures became the source of the Vṛṣṇi race.

sanskrit: ete prajānāṃ patayaḥ samuddiṣṭā yaśasvinaḥ ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi devāṃs tribhuvaneśvarān
english: These illustrious ones have been recounted as the Lords of Creatures; now hereafter I shall declare the gods, the sovereigns of the three worlds.

sanskrit: bhago 'ṃśaś cāryamā caiva mitro 'tha varuṇas tathā savitā caiva dhātā ca vivasvāṃś ca mahābalaḥ
english: Bhaga and Aṃśa, and Aryaman, and Mitra, and Varuṇa likewise, and Savitṛ, and Dhātṛ, and the mighty Vivasvant —

sanskrit: pūṣā tvaṣṭā tathaivendro dvādaśo viṣṇur ucyate ta ete dvādaśādityāḥ kaśyapasyātmasaṃbhavāḥ
english: Pūṣan, Tvaṣṭṛ, and likewise Indra — and Viṣṇu is called the twelfth: these are the twelve Ādityas, sprung from the very self of Kaśyapa.

sanskrit: nāsatyaś caiva dasraś ca smṛtau dvāv aśvināv api mārtāṇḍasyātmajāv etāv aṣṭamasya prajāpateḥ
english: Nāsatya and Dasra too are remembered as the two Aśvins; these two are the sons of Mārtāṇḍa, the eighth Lord of Creatures.

sanskrit: tvaṣṭuś caivātmajaḥ śrīmān viśvarūpo mahāyaśāḥ ajaikapād ahirbudhnyo virūpākṣo 'tha raivataḥ
english: And the glorious, far-famed Viśvarūpa was the son of Tvaṣṭṛ; then Ajaikapād, Ahirbudhnya, Virūpākṣa, and Raivata —

sanskrit: haraś ca bahurūpaś ca tryambakaś ca sureśvaraḥ sāvitraś ca jayantaś ca pinākī cāparājitaḥ pūrvam eva mahābhāgā vasavo 'ṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ
english: And Hara, and Bahurūpa, and Tryambaka the lord of gods, and Sāvitra, and Jayanta, and the bow-bearing Aparājita: these are the Rudras. And earlier the eight illustrious Vasus were proclaimed.

sanskrit: eta evaṃvidhā devā manor eva prajāpateḥ te ca pūrve surāś ceti dvividhāḥ pitaraḥ smṛtāḥ
english: These gods of such a kind are sprung from Manu, the Lord of Creatures; and the Ancestors are remembered as twofold — the former ones, and the gods as well.

sanskrit: śīlarūparatās tv anye tathānye siddhasādhyayoḥ ṛbhavo marutaś caiva devānāṃ coditā gaṇāḥ
english: Some others delight in virtue and beauty, and others belong to the Siddhas and Sādhyas; and the Ṛbhus and the Maruts too are reckoned hosts of the gods.

sanskrit: evam ete samāmnātā viśvedevās tathāśvinau ādityāḥ kṣatriyās teṣāṃ viśas tu marutas tathā
english: Thus have these been enumerated — the Viśvedevas and likewise the Aśvins. Among them the Ādityas are the warriors, and the Maruts the commoners.

sanskrit: aśvinau tu matau śūdrau tapasy ugre samāhitau smṛtās tv aṅgiraso devā brāhmaṇā iti niścayaḥ ity etat sarvadevānāṃ cāturvarṇyaṃ prakīrtitam
english: The two Aśvins are held to be Śūdras, intent upon fierce austerity; and the Aṅgirasa gods are remembered, by settled judgment, to be Brāhmaṇas. Thus the fourfold order of all the gods has been proclaimed.

sanskrit: etān vai prātar utthāya devān yas tu prakīrtayet svajād anyakṛtāc caiva sarvapāpāt pramucyate
english: Whoever, rising at dawn, glorifies these gods is released from every sin — both that done by himself and that done by another.

sanskrit: yavakrīto 'tha raibhyaś ca arvāvasuparāvasū auśijaś caiva kakṣīvān nalaś cāṅgirasaḥ sutāḥ
english: Yavakrīta, and Raibhya, and Arvāvasu and Parāvasu, and Auśija, and Kakṣīvant, and Nala — these are sons of Aṅgiras.

sanskrit: ṛṣer medhātitheḥ putraḥ kaṇvo barhiṣadas tathā trailokyabhāvanās tāta prācyāṃ saptarṣayas tathā
english: Kaṇva, the son of the sage Medhātithi, and likewise Barhiṣad — these, my son, are fashioners of the three worlds, the seven seers in the eastern quarter.

sanskrit: unmuco vimucaś caiva svastyātreyaś ca vīryavān pramucaś cedhmavāhaś ca bhagavāṃś ca dṛḍhavrataḥ
english: Unmuca and Vimuca, and the valiant Svastyātreya, and Pramuca, and Idhmavāha, and the lord of firm vows —

sanskrit: mitrāvaruṇayoḥ putras tathāgastyaḥ pratāpavān ete brahmarṣayo nityam āśritā dakṣiṇāṃ diśam
english: And the majestic Agastya, son of Mitra and Varuṇa — these are the Brahman-seers, forever stationed in the southern quarter.

sanskrit: ruṣadguḥ kavaṣo dhaumyaḥ parivyādhaś ca vīryavān ekataś ca dvitaś caiva tritaś caiva maharṣayaḥ
english: Ruṣadgu, Kavaṣa, Dhaumya, and the valiant Parivyādha, and Ekata, and Dvita, and Trita — these are the great seers.

sanskrit: atreḥ putraś ca bhagavāṃs tathā sārasvataḥ prabhuḥ ete nava mahātmānaḥ paścimām āśritā diśam
english: And the lord, the son of Atri, and likewise the mighty Sārasvata — these nine great-souled ones are stationed in the western quarter.

sanskrit: ātreyaś ca vasiṣṭhaś ca kaśyapaś ca mahān ṛṣiḥ gautamaḥ sabharadvājo viśvāmitro 'tha kauśikaḥ
english: Ātreya, and Vasiṣṭha, and Kaśyapa the great seer, and Gautama, with Bharadvāja, and Viśvāmitra the Kauśika —

sanskrit: tathaiva putro bhagavān ṛcīkasya mahātmanaḥ jamadagniś ca saptaite udīcīṃ diśam āśritāḥ
english: And likewise the lord Jamadagni, son of the great-souled Ṛcīka — these seven are stationed in the northern quarter.

sanskrit: ete pratidiśaṃ sarve kīrtitās tigmatejasaḥ sākṣibhūtā mahātmāno bhuvanānāṃ prabhāvanāḥ
english: All these, of keen splendour, have been recounted in each quarter — great-souled ones who stand as witnesses and as fashioners of the worlds.

sanskrit: evam ete mahātmānaḥ sthitāḥ pratyekaśo diśaḥ eteṣāṃ kīrtanaṃ kṛtvā sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: Thus these great-souled ones are stationed, each in their several quarters; by uttering praise of them a man is released from all his sins.

sanskrit: yasyāṃ yasyāṃ diśi hy ete tāṃ diśaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ mucyate sarvapāpebhyaḥ svastimāṃś ca gṛhān vrajet
english: In whatever quarter these dwell, the man who takes refuge in that quarter is freed from all his sins, and may go home in safety and well-being.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca pitāmaha mahāprājña yudhi satyaparākrama śrotum icchāmi kārtsnyena kṛṣṇam avyayam īśvaram
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O grandsire, deeply wise, whose valour in battle is unfailing as truth, I wish to hear in full of Kṛṣṇa, the undecaying Lord.

sanskrit: yac cāsya tejaḥ sumahad yac ca karma purātanam tan me sarvaṃ yathātattvaṃ prabrūhi bharatarṣabha
english: His most vast splendour, and his deeds of old — tell me all of that as it truly is, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: tiryagyonigataṃ rūpaṃ kathaṃ dhāritavān hariḥ kena kāryavisargeṇa tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: How did Hari come to bear a form born in the animal womb, and for the accomplishing of what task? Tell me that, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca purāhaṃ mṛgayāṃ yāto mārkaṇḍeyāśrame sthitaḥ tatrāpaśyaṃ munigaṇān samāsīnān sahasraśaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Long ago, having gone out hunting, I halted at the hermitage of Mārkaṇḍeya; there I beheld hosts of sages seated by the thousand.

sanskrit: tatas te madhuparkeṇa pūjāṃ cakrur atho mayi pratigṛhya ca tāṃ pūjāṃ pratyanandam ṛṣīn aham
english: Then they did me honour with the madhuparka offering; and having accepted that honour, I in turn greeted the seers with gladness.

sanskrit: kathaiṣā kathitā tatra kaśyapena maharṣiṇā manaḥprahlādinīṃ divyāṃ tām ihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu
english: There this tale was told by the great seer Kaśyapa — a divine tale that gladdens the heart; hear it now with single mind.

sanskrit: purā dānavamukhyā hi krodhalobhasamanvitāḥ balena mattāḥ śataśo narakādyā mahāsurāḥ
english: In olden times the foremost of the Dānavas, filled with wrath and greed, drunk with might by the hundred — great Asuras led by Naraka —

sanskrit: tathaiva cānye bahavo dānavā yuddhadurmadāḥ na sahante sma devānāṃ samṛddhiṃ tām anuttamām
english: and likewise many other Dānavas, mad for battle, could not endure that unsurpassed prosperity of the gods.

sanskrit: dānavair ardyamānās tu devā devarṣayas tathā na śarma lebhire rājan viśamānās tatas tataḥ
english: Tormented by the Dānavas, the gods and the divine seers found no refuge, O king, but scattered hither and thither.

sanskrit: pṛthivīṃ cārtarūpāṃ te samapaśyan divaukasaḥ dānavair abhisaṃkīrṇāṃ ghorarūpair mahābalaiḥ bhārārtām apakṛṣṭāṃ ca duḥkhitāṃ saṃnimajjatīm
english: And the dwellers of heaven beheld the earth in the very shape of anguish — overrun by mighty Dānavas of dreadful form, oppressed by her burden, dragged down, suffering, and sinking away.

sanskrit: athāditeyāḥ saṃtrastā brahmāṇam idam abruvan kathaṃ śakyāmahe brahman dānavair upamardanam
english: Then the sons of Aditi, sore afraid, spoke thus to Brahmā: How, O Brahman, can we endure this crushing by the Dānavas?

sanskrit: svayaṃbhūs tān uvācedaṃ nisṛṣṭo 'tra vidhir mayā te vareṇābhisaṃmattā balena ca madena ca
english: The Self-Born said this to them: The ordinance has been set forth here by me. They are drunk with their boon, with their might, and with their arrogance;

sanskrit: nāvabhotsyanti saṃmūḍhā viṣṇum avyaktadarśanam varāharūpiṇaṃ devam adhṛṣyam amarair api
english: in their utter delusion they will not perceive Viṣṇu, whose vision is hidden — the god in the form of a boar, unassailable even by the immortals.

sanskrit: eṣa vegena gatvā hi yatra te dānavādhamāḥ antarbhūmigatā ghorā nivasanti sahasraśaḥ śamayiṣyati śrutvā te jahṛṣuḥ surasattamāḥ
english: Going swiftly to where those vilest of Dānavas, dreadful ones, dwell by the thousand deep within the earth, he will quell them. Hearing this, those best of the gods rejoiced.

sanskrit: tato viṣṇur mahātejā vārāhaṃ rūpam āśritaḥ antarbhūmiṃ saṃpraviśya jagāma ditijān prati
english: Then Viṣṇu, of vast splendour, assuming the form of a boar, entered deep within the earth and went forth against the sons of Diti.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca sahitāḥ sarve daityāḥ sattvam amānuṣam prasahya sahasā sarve saṃtasthuḥ kālamohitāḥ
english: And beholding that more-than-mortal being, all the Daityas together, bewildered by destiny, rose up at once with sudden force and made their stand.

sanskrit: sarve ca samabhidrutya varāhaṃ jagṛhuḥ samam saṃkruddhāś ca varāhaṃ taṃ vyakarṣanta samantataḥ
english: And all together they rushed upon the boar and seized him as one, and in their fury they dragged that boar this way and that on every side.

sanskrit: dānavendrā mahākāyā mahāvīryā balocchritāḥ nāśaknuvaṃś ca kiṃ cit te tasya kartuṃ tadā vibho
english: Those lords of the Dānavas, of huge frame, mighty valour, and towering strength, were yet unable to do him any harm at all, O mighty one.

sanskrit: tato 'gaman vismayaṃ te dānavendrā bhayāt tadā saṃśayaṃ gatam ātmānaṃ menire ca sahasraśaḥ
english: Then those lords of the Dānavas fell into wonder, and then, from fear, by the thousand they deemed their own selves brought to peril.

sanskrit: tato devādidevaḥ sa yogātmā yogasārathiḥ yogam āsthāya bhagavāṃs tadā bharatasattama
english: Then that foremost god of gods, whose self is yoga, the charioteer of yoga, the Lord, taking his stand in yoga, O best of the Bhāratas —

sanskrit: vinanāda mahānādaṃ kṣobhayan daityadānavān saṃnāditā yena lokāḥ sarvāś caiva diśo daśa
english: roared out a mighty roar, throwing the Daityas and Dānavas into turmoil — a roar by which all the worlds and all the ten quarters were made to resound.

sanskrit: tena saṃnādaśabdena lokāḥ saṃkṣobham āgaman saṃbhrāntāś ca diśaḥ sarvā devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ
english: By the sound of that roar the worlds were thrown into commotion, and all the quarters were confounded, and the gods with Śakra at their head.

sanskrit: nirviceṣṭaṃ jagac cāpi babhūvātibhṛśaṃ tadā sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ caiva tena nādena mohitam
english: And the whole universe then became utterly without motion, all that is fixed and all that moves alike, stupefied by that roar.

sanskrit: tatas te dānavāḥ sarve tena śabdena bhīṣitāḥ petur gatāsavaś caiva viṣṇutejovimohitāḥ
english: Then all those Dānavas, terrified by that sound and overwhelmed by the splendour of Viṣṇu, fell down with their breath gone out of them.

sanskrit: rasātalagatāṃś caiva varāhas tridaśadviṣaḥ khuraiḥ saṃdārayām āsa māṃsamedosthisaṃcayam
english: And those foes of the gods who had fled to the nether world the boar tore apart with his hooves — their heaped-up mass of flesh and fat and bone.

sanskrit: nādena tena mahatā sanātana iti smṛtaḥ padmanābho mahāyogī bhūtācāryaḥ sa bhūtarāṭ
english: By that mighty roar he came to be remembered as the Eternal — the lotus-naveled, the great yogin, the teacher of beings, the king of beings.

sanskrit: tato devagaṇāḥ sarve pitāmaham upābruvan nādo 'yaṃ kīdṛśo deva nainaṃ vidma vayaṃ vibho ko 'sau hi kasya vā nādo yena vihvalitaṃ jagat
english: Then all the hosts of gods spoke to the grandsire: What manner of roar is this, O god? We do not know it, O mighty one. Who is he, or whose is this roar, by which the universe is thrown into distress?

sanskrit: etasminn antare viṣṇur vārāhaṃ rūpam āsthitaḥ udatiṣṭhan mahādevaḥ stūyamāno maharṣibhiḥ
english: In that very interval Viṣṇu, abiding in his boar-form — the great god — rose up, being praised by the great seers.

sanskrit: pitāmaha uvāca nihatya dānavapatīn mahāvarṣmā mahābalaḥ eṣa devo mahāyogī bhūtātmā bhūtabhāvanaḥ
english: The grandsire said: Having slain the lords of the Dānavas, this god of vast frame and mighty strength — the great yogin, the Self of beings, the begetter of beings —

sanskrit: sarvabhūteśvaro yogī yonir ātmā tathātmanaḥ sthirībhavata kṛṣṇo 'yaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanaḥ
english: is the lord of all beings, the yogin, the womb and the Self even of the Self. Be steadfast: this is Kṛṣṇa, the destroyer of all sin.

sanskrit: kṛtvā karmātisādhv etad aśakyam amitaprabhaḥ samāyātaḥ svam ātmānaṃ mahābhāgo mahādyutiḥ padmanābho mahāyogī bhūtātmā bhūtabhāvanaḥ
english: Having done this most excellent deed that none could do, he of boundless radiance, illustrious and of great brilliance, has returned into his own Self — the lotus-naveled, the great yogin, the Self of beings, the begetter of beings.

sanskrit: na saṃtāpo na bhīḥ kāryā śoko vā surasattamāḥ vidhir eṣa prabhāvaś ca kālaḥ saṃkṣayakārakaḥ lokān dhārayatānena nādo mukto mahātmanā
english: No grief, no fear, no sorrow should be felt, O best of the gods; this is the ordinance and the power, and Time the worker of dissolution. By this great-souled one, who upholds the worlds, the roar was let forth.

sanskrit: sa eva hi mahābhāgaḥ sarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ acyutaḥ puṇḍarīkākṣaḥ sarvabhūtasamudbhavaḥ
english: For he indeed is the illustrious one, adored by all the worlds — the undecaying, the lotus-eyed, the origin of all beings.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yogaṃ me paramaṃ tāta mokṣasya vada bhārata tam ahaṃ tattvato jñātum icchāmi vadatāṃ vara
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Tell me, my father, the supreme yoga of liberation, O scion of Bharata; I wish to know it in its truth, O best of those who speak.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam saṃvādaṃ mokṣasaṃyuktaṃ śiṣyasya guruṇā saha
english: Bhīṣma said: On this point too they recount this ancient tale — a dialogue concerning liberation between a pupil and his teacher.

sanskrit: kaś cid brāhmaṇam āsīnam ācāryam ṛṣisattamam śiṣyaḥ paramamedhāvī śreyorthī susamāhitaḥ caraṇāv upasaṃgṛhya sthitaḥ prāñjalir abravīt
english: A certain pupil, of supreme intelligence, seeking the highest good and fully composed, having clasped the feet of a Brāhmaṇa, his teacher and the best of seers, who sat there, stood with joined palms and spoke.

sanskrit: upāsanāt prasanno 'si yadi vai bhagavan mama saṃśayo me mahān kaś cit tan me vyākhyātum arhasi
english: If, O lord, you are pleased with my service, there is a certain great doubt of mine; this you ought to explain to me.

sanskrit: kutaś cāhaṃ kutaś ca tvaṃ tat samyag brūhi yat param kathaṃ ca sarvabhūteṣu sameṣu dvijasattama samyagvṛttā nivartante viparītāḥ kṣayodayāḥ
english: Whence am I, and whence are you? Tell me rightly that which is highest; and how, O best of the twice-born, among all beings that are alike, do their rightly-ordered courses turn back, and their decline and rise prove contrary?

sanskrit: vedeṣu cāpi yad vākyaṃ laukikaṃ vyāpakaṃ ca yat etad vidvan yathātattvaṃ sarvaṃ vyākhyātum arhasi
english: And the word that is in the Vedas, and that which is worldly and all-pervading — all this, O learned one, you ought to expound as it truly is.

sanskrit: gurur uvāca śṛṇu śiṣya mahāprājña brahmaguhyam idaṃ param adhyātmaṃ sarvabhūtānām āgamānāṃ ca yad vasu
english: The teacher said: Hear, O pupil of great wisdom, this supreme mystery of Brahman — the inmost Self of all beings, and that which is the treasure of the scriptures.

sanskrit: vāsudevaḥ sarvam idaṃ viśvasya brahmaṇo mukham satyaṃ dānam atho yajñas titikṣā dama ārjavam
english: Vāsudeva is all this; he is the mouth of Brahman, the universe. Truth, giving, and sacrifice, forbearance, self-restraint, and uprightness —

sanskrit: puruṣaṃ sanātanaṃ viṣṇuṃ yat tad vedavido viduḥ sargapralayakartāram avyaktaṃ brahma śāśvatam tad idaṃ brahma vārṣṇeyam itihāsaṃ śṛṇuṣva me
english: That which the knowers of the Veda know as the eternal Person, Viṣṇu — the maker of creation and dissolution, the unmanifest, the everlasting Brahman — this Brahman is of the Vṛṣṇi; hear from me the tale of it.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo brāhmaṇaiḥ śrāvyo rājanyaḥ kṣatriyais tathā māhātmyaṃ devadevasya viṣṇor amitatejasaḥ arhas tvam asi kalyāṇa vārṣṇeyaṃ śṛṇu yat param
english: The greatness of Viṣṇu, the god of gods, of measureless splendour, should be made to be heard by Brāhmaṇas for a Brāhmaṇa, and by Kṣatriyas for one of royal birth. You, O blessed one, are worthy of it; hear that which is supreme, the tale of the Vṛṣṇi.

sanskrit: kālacakram anādyantaṃ bhāvābhāvasvalakṣaṇam trailokyaṃ sarvabhūteṣu cakravat parivartate
english: The wheel of Time, without beginning or end, marked by being and non-being, turns round like a wheel through the three worlds among all beings.

sanskrit: yat tad akṣaram avyaktam amṛtaṃ brahma śāśvatam vadanti puruṣavyāghraṃ keśavaṃ puruṣarṣabham
english: That which is the imperishable, the unmanifest, the immortal, the everlasting Brahman — that they declare to be Keśava, the tiger among men, the bull among men.

sanskrit: pitṝn devān ṛṣīṃś caiva tathā vai yakṣadānavān nāgāsuramanuṣyāṃś ca sṛjate paramo 'vyayaḥ
english: The supreme, the undecaying, creates the Ancestors, the gods, and the seers, and likewise the Yakṣas and Dānavas, the Nāgas, Asuras, and human beings.

sanskrit: tathaiva vedaśāstrāṇi lokadharmāṃś ca śāśvatān pralaye prakṛtiṃ prāpya yugādau sṛjate prabhuḥ
english: And likewise the Vedas and the sciences, and the everlasting laws of the world — these, at the dissolution, having reached primordial Nature, the Lord creates again at the dawn of the age.

sanskrit: yathartuṣv ṛtuliṅgāni nānārūpāṇi paryaye dṛśyante tāni tāny eva tathā brahmāharātriṣu
english: As in the seasons the marks of the seasons, in their various forms, are seen — those very same ones again in their turning — so it is in the days and nights of Brahmā.

sanskrit: atha yad yad yadā bhāvi kālayogād yugādiṣu tat tad utpadyate jñānaṃ lokayātrāvidhānajam
english: Now whatever is to come to be, by the conjunction of Time, at the beginnings of the ages — that very knowledge arises, born of the ordering of the world's course.

sanskrit: yugānte 'ntarhitān vedān setihāsān maharṣayaḥ lebhire tapasā pūrvam anujñātāḥ svayaṃbhuvā
english: The Vedas, vanished at the age's end, together with the histories, the great seers regained of old through austerity, permitted thereto by the Self-Born.

sanskrit: vedavid veda bhagavān vedāṅgāni bṛhaspatiḥ bhārgavo nītiśāstraṃ ca jagāda jagato hitam
english: The lord, the knower of the Veda, knows the Veda; Bṛhaspati declared the limbs of the Veda; and the Bhārgava declared the science of statecraft, for the good of the world.

sanskrit: gāndharvaṃ nārado vedaṃ bharadvājo dhanurgraham devarṣicaritaṃ gārgyaḥ kṛṣṇātreyaś cikitsitam
english: Nārada declared the lore of the Gandharvas, Bharadvāja the wielding of the bow, Gārgya the deeds of the divine seers, and Kṛṣṇātreya the art of healing.

sanskrit: nyāyatantrāṇy anekāni tais tair uktāni vādibhiḥ hetvāgamasadācārair yad uktaṃ tad upāsyate
english: Many systems of reasoning were set forth by various disputants; what is propounded in accordance with logic, scripture, and right conduct — that is held in honour.
